subject: Long et al. (2016)
object: Long et al. (2016) reported a girl of white European ancestry who was diagnosed with fetal cardiomegaly at 30 weeks' gestation and was delivered 1 week later because of fetal hydrops. After birth, echocardiography showed severe enlargement of both ventricles and both atria, severe systolic dysfunction (LVEF 25%), a small apical ventricular septal defect, and a moderate secundum atrial septal defect. She also had bilateral cataracts and mild facial dysmorphism: wide-set eyes, downslanting palpebral fissures, prominent forehead, mild macrocephaly, and low-set ears. Extensive metabolic and genetic testing did not find a cause, and echocardiograms showed that her parents did not have asymptomatic DCM.

subject: Long et al. (2016)
object: Long et al. (2016) reported that the patient needed 2 months in hospital for prematurity and heart failure, and her systolic function improved on medical therapy. At 4 months of age she received a gastrostomy tube for oral aversion and failure to thrive. Her cardiac function then declined gradually, and at 21 months she was admitted twice for decompensated heart failure (LVEF 22%) with restrictive physiology. During these admissions she had transient hypoglycemia, elevated lactate, and very high transaminases, which the authors attributed to low cardiac output and congestive hepatopathy. Skin and muscle biopsies showed no respiratory chain or mitochondrial DNA abnormalities. She died at 22 months of age of multisystem organ failure due to end-stage heart failure.

subject: Long et al. (2016)
object: Clinical exome sequencing of the patient alone found no cause. Long et al. (2016) then performed trio-based whole-exome sequencing and identified a de novo heterozygous c.224C>A (NM_022157.3) mutation in RRAGC, resulting in a ser75-to-tyr (S75Y) substitution in the highly conserved P-loop of the GTPase domain. Sanger sequencing confirmed the mutation. SIFT and PolyPhen2 predicted it to be damaging, and it was absent from ExAC. ExAC controls had no missense or truncating variants in the RRAGC GTPase domain. In silico modeling predicted that the mutation would disrupt Mg(2+) and ligand coordination and cause conformational expansion of the GDP-bound state.

subject: Long et al. (2016)
object: Long et al. (2016) overexpressed RagC(S75Y) in AD293 cells. Compared with wildtype RagC, the mutant partly prevented the loss of S6K and S6 phosphorylation during amino acid starvation, showing increased mTORC1 signaling. The authors concluded that the mutation is gain-of-function and activates mTORC1.

subject: Kim et al. (2021)
object: Kim et al. (2021) noted that whole exome sequencing of a pediatric dilated cardiomyopathy (DCM) patient had previously identified a de novo S75Y variant in Rag GTPase protein C (RagC, RRAGC), revealing RRAGC as a new susceptibility gene, and stated that further evidence including functional studies in animal models was required to prove pathogenicity.

subject: Kim et al. (2021)
object: Kim et al. (2021) reviewed that the S75 residue of RagC is evolutionarily conserved from yeast to human and lies in the phosphate-binding loop (P-loop) motif mediating GTP/GDP binding, that recurrent somatic RRAGC S75 mutations (S75C, S75N, S75F) occur in follicular lymphoma with greater GDP-binding affinity and hyperactive mTORC1 signaling, and that in silico protein modeling predicted S75Y also increases the GDP-bound state, supporting a gain-of-function mechanism.

subject: Kim et al. (2021)
object: Kim et al. (2021) generated a zebrafish rragca S56Y knock-in line (corresponding to human RagC S75Y) by TALEN-mediated editing, introducing a C-to-A conversion confirmed by Sanger sequencing and tracked by a newly created RsaI site; homozygous rragc KI fish had unchanged rragca mRNA levels in adult hearts.

subject: Kim et al. (2021)
object: Kim et al. (2021) found that rragc S56Y knock-in zebrafish began to die at 5 months with about 70% surviving to 1 year, had reduced body weight and reduced maximum swimming capacity, and showed ventricular systolic dysfunction with reduced ejection fraction and fractional shortening, increased end-systolic volume/body weight ratio, decreased E/A ratio, increased myocardial performance index, enlarged ventricular surface area/body weight, reduced trabecular density, and elevated ventricular myosin heavy chain (vmhc) transcript, which the authors concluded confirmed pathogenicity of the S75Y variant.

subject: Kim et al. (2021)
object: Kim et al. (2021) obtained two rragca knockout alleles as byproducts of the knock-in approach (a 124-bp insertion in exon 1 causing a premature stop codon with 60% reduction of rragca transcripts, and a 10-nucleotide deletion also predicted to truncate the protein); homozygotes for either allele showed no noticeable phenotype up to at least 1 year of age and preserved cardiac pump function, demonstrating that knock-in but not knockout recapitulated cardiomyopathy and supporting a gain-of-function mechanism.

subject: Kim et al. (2021)
object: Kim et al. (2021) showed that adenoviral overexpression of RagCS75Y, but not wild-type RagC, increased neonatal rat ventricular cardiomyocyte size 1.5-fold and raised hypertrophic markers Nppa, Nppb and Mhc7 with downregulation of Mhc6, indicating that the pathogenicity of the S75Y variant is conserved and recapitulated in vitro.

subject: Kim et al. (2021)
object: Kim et al. (2021) found that RagCS75Y-expressing cardiomyocytes had hyperactive mTORC1 signaling (increased P-p70S6K and P-S6), reduced TFEB with a higher-molecular-weight band retained in the cytoplasmic rather than nuclear fraction, reduced TFEB target gene expression, blunted LC3-II induction by fasting or bafilomycin-A1, accumulation of ubiquitin-conjugated proteins in the insoluble fraction and more aggresomes, indicating insufficient autophagy flux.

subject: Kim et al. (2021)
object: Kim et al. (2021) showed that rragc S56Y knock-in zebrafish hearts recapitulated the cellular findings, with downregulated TFEB-controlled lysosomal genes, severely reduced LC3-II unresponsive to bafilomycin-A1, elevated ubiquitin-conjugated proteins, and significantly increased glycogen deposits on Periodic Acid-Schiff staining at 1 year of age; the authors concluded that RagCS75Y cardiomyopathy is characterized by dysregulated autophagy-lysosomal clearance and glycogen deposition with both mTORC1 activation and TFEB inhibition.

subject: Kim et al. (2021)
object: Kim et al. (2021) found that although TFEB phosphorylation at the mTORC1 site S211 was increased in RagCS75Y cells and was attenuated by rapamycin, rapamycin did not promote TFEB nuclear translocation; co-immunoprecipitation in AD293 cells revealed greater binding between RagCS75Y and TFEB than between RagCWT and TFEB that was not reduced by rapamycin, leading the authors to propose that mTOR-independent binding of RagCS75Y to TFEB restricts TFEB nuclear translocation and is the key pathological event leading to cardiomyopathy.

subject: Kim et al. (2021)
object: Kim et al. (2021) reported that mTOR inhibition was ineffective against RagCS75Y cardiomyopathy: 24-hour rapamycin or torin treatment failed to normalize enlarged RagCS75Y cardiomyocyte size despite drastic suppression of mTORC1 activity, and mtor haploinsufficiency in rragc KI;mtor+/- double mutant zebrafish failed to improve cardiac pump dysfunction, vmhc marker expression, growth, or survival.

subject: Kim et al. (2021)
object: Kim et al. (2021) showed that TFEB activation ameliorated RagCS75Y cardiomyopathy: ectopic TFEB expression normalized the enlarged cardiomyocyte size, and a cardiomyocyte-specific Tg(cmlc2:tfeb-GFP) transgene expressing tfeb 9-fold above wild type restored ejection fraction, fractional shortening and vmhc expression and significantly improved survival in rragc KI fish, with exogenous TFEB detected in nuclei and restoration of autophagy flux, leading the authors to conclude that TFEB activation, but not mTOR inhibition, is therapeutic.

subject: Kim et al. (2021)
object: Kim et al. (2021) concluded from combined in vivo and in vitro evidence that S75Y is a pathogenic gain-of-function mutation in RagC that leads to cardiomyopathy, with defective mTOR-TFEB signaling as a primary pathological step, and noted that it remains to be determined whether follicular lymphoma occurs in RagCS75Y cardiomyopathy patients.

subject: Reijnders et al. (2023)
object: Reijnders et al. (2023) reported 3 infants with dilated cardiomyopathy, hepatopathy, and brain abnormalities, including pachygyria, polymicrogyria, and septo-optic dysplasia. The authors described the disorder as an early-onset mTORopathy with an unfavorable prognosis.

subject: Reijnders et al. (2023)
object: In an infant with this disorder, Reijnders et al. (2023) used trio exome sequencing to identify a de novo heterozygous missense variant in the RRAGC gene, c.269C>A (p.Thr90Asn). This variant had previously been reported as a somatic variant in follicular lymphoma. Patient fibroblasts carrying the variant showed increased cell size, dysregulated p70S6K and TFEB signaling, and mTOR subcellular localization that was decoupled from metabolic state. The authors concluded that these findings were in line with constitutive overactivation of mTORC1.

subject: Reijnders et al. (2023)
object: In an infant with this disorder, Reijnders et al. (2023) identified a de novo heterozygous missense variant in the RRAGC gene, c.353C>T (p.Pro118Leu), by trio exome sequencing. The variant had previously been reported as a somatic variant in follicular lymphoma, and the key cellular findings were confirmed in a HEK293 cell model.

subject: Reijnders et al. (2023)
object: In an infant with this disorder, Reijnders et al. (2023) identified a de novo heterozygous missense variant in the RRAGC gene, c.343T>C (p.Trp115Arg), by trio exome sequencing. The variant had previously been reported as a somatic variant in follicular lymphoma, and the key cellular findings were confirmed in a HEK293 cell model.

subject: Reijnders et al. (2023)
object: Reijnders et al. (2023) concluded that the cellular findings for all 3 RRAGC variants were in line with constitutive overactivation of the mTORC1 pathway. They showed this in patient fibroblasts and confirmed it in HEK293 cells.
